full_judgment: 5. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State, submits that the activities of the detenu as detailed in the grounds of detention, Annexure-'B' fall within the definition of "Prejudicial acts" as contemplated under section 2(f) (ii) and (viii) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. He submits that the Government may direct any person to be detained and the powers vested in the Government under section 3(i)(a) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 is without any limitation. Similarly, under section 3(2) of the Special Powers Act, the District Magistrate or the Additional District Magistrate who is empowered to pass an order of detention may direct detention of a person without fixing any time limit whatsoever but if the District Magistrate or/the Additional District Magistrate passes an order of detention beyond 30 days, such an order shall not remain in force for more the 30 days after the making thereof unless in the meantime it has been approved by the Government under section 3(3) of the Special Powers Act. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam further submits that in case of detention exceeding 120 days the Government shall place the records before the Advisory Board within one hundred and twenty days from the date of detention as required under section 10. As per section 11 of the Special Powers Act the Advisory Board shall submit its report to the Government within one hundred and seventy days from the date of detention. Under section 11 the Advisory Board shall submit its report to the Government within 170 days from the date of detention incorporated there in its view if there is sufficient cause for further detention and the Government shall take appropriate action upon the report under section 12. The Advisory Board shall, after affording the person concerned an opportunity of being heard in person, review such detention order, unless revoked earlier, once in every six months from the date of such detention order and the Government shall inform the person concerned of the result of such review. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, however, finds difficulty in supporting the legality of extension of detention of the detenu by the Government under section 3(3) by the order dated 30.7.95 (Annexure-'C')
